Wealth: Wealth comes to you as ground. You add to it the way soil takes a season, layer on layer, and it holds because you keep checking the field's edge. The danger is loving the pile more than the point of it. The harvest is worth more feeding the table than padding the ledger.
Savings: This energy is built for savings. You set a portion aside before spending it, and it compounds into a floor under everything else you build. Hoarded past use, it turns to ground kept only for its weight. A season with nothing spent on purpose is a season only half kept.
Steady love: Steadiness is how this energy loves. You build it the slow way, laying trust down like ground that needs time before anything sits steady on it, though the same patience can read to a partner as coldness. The plain thing said out loud, on purpose, costs less than the silence that stands in for it.
